In mathematics, a '''Rickart space''' (after [[Charles Earl Rickart]]), also called a '''basically disconnected space''', is a [[topological space]] in which open σ-compact subsets have [[compact space|compact]] open closures. 

{{harvtxt|Grove|Pedersen|1984}} named them after {{harvs|txt|first=C. E. |last=Rickart|year=1946}}, who showed that Rickart spaces are related to monotone σ-complete [[C*-algebra]]s under [[Gelfand duality]], in the same way that  [[Stonean space]]s are related to [[AW*-algebra]]s. 

Rickart spaces were also studied by [[Paul Halmos]] under the name ''Boolean σ-spaces'', as they correspond to Boolean σ-algebras via [[Stone duality]].<ref>See Section 22, specifically Theorem 12, in {{harvtxt|Halmos|1974}}.</ref>
The concept of Rickart spaces resurfaced in {{harvtxt|Jamneshan|Tao|2023}} under the name ''Stone<sub>σ</sub>-spaces''. 

Both algebraic descriptions (namely, the [[C*-algebra|C*-algebraic]] and [[Boolean algebra|Boolean algebraic]] ones) are explicitly discussed in {{harvtxt|Fritz|Lorenzin|2025}}.<ref>See Corollary 2.1.17 and Fact 3.1.10. </ref>

Rickart spaces are [[totally disconnected]] and [[sub-Stonean space]]s.
